texts.facts: BRIEF FACTS: 1. Detailed Accident Report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act in respect of injuries sustained by Sh. Arun Katariya (hereinafter called the claimant) on account of alleged rash and negligent driving of vehicle bearing Arun Katariya (Dar) vs Rajender Singh (290/21, Crp) on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34909065/ 1 Registration No. HR 38 D 6294 (hereinafter called the offending vehicle) driven by Sh. Rajender Singh (hereinafter called the Respondent No.1) and owned by Sh. Alok Goel (hereinafter called the Respondent No.2) and insured with The Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. (hereinafter called the insurance company), which is being treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. 2. Preliminary information regarding accident in question was received at PS C.R. Park on 21.09.2021 at about 11.50 a.m., when complainant Sh.Arun S/o Sh. Mukesh came at the Police Station and gave a statement that on 14.09.2021, he was travelling as a labourer on Truck bearing Registration No. HE38S 6292, driven by Sh.Rajender for unloading the bricks at I-Block, C.R. Park, New Delhi and while returning back around 9.30 a.m., upon the asking of driver Rajender, he tried to untangle the cable wires and branch of a tree by his left hand while putting his right hand on Tail Gate (Dala), the driver Rajender drove the vehicle without informing him and without taking care that he has removed his hand or not, that his right hand got stuck between the Tail Gate and tree causing serious injuries on his fingers upon which driver Rajender simply offloaded him and fled away from MACT No. 738/22 Arun Kataria vs. Rajender Singh Page No. 2 of 42 the spot. He contended that the injuries were caused to him on account of sheer reckless driving on the part of driver Rajender. He also stated that he was treated at Safdarjung Hospital vide MLC No. 264884/2021. He explained that driver Rajender had undertaken to bear the expenses of his treatment but later he refused to do which is why he has come to Police Station for making a complaint. FIR was registered. Notice under Section 133 M. V. Act was given to the owner of the Truck, who confirmed that the Truck was being driven by Rajender Singh. Documents pertaining to the Truck were also handed over and found to be in order. The offending vehicle was seized and got mechanically inspected. Subsequently upon conclusion of investigation, charge sheet was filed before concerned criminal court while DAR was filed before this Tribunal. 3. Copy of DAR was supplied to driver/R-1 whereas R-2/ owner chose not to appear despite service. REPLY 4. In written statement filed on behalf of R-1 and R-2, it is stated that R-1/driver has been falsely implicated as he was not negligent in driving the vehicle at the time of accident. It is further mentioned that injures were caused to the claimant due to his own negligence as he fell down during the course of unloading of bricks. It is further stated that R-1 had a valid driving license as on the date of accident, while the alleged offending vehicle was duly insured, as verified by the Arun Katariya (Dar) vs Rajender Singh (290/21, Crp) on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34909065/ 2 Investigating Officer during investigation. 5. In the written statement filed on behalf of insurance MACT No. 738/22 Arun Kataria vs. Rajender Singh Page No. 3 of 42 company, it is stated that the insured vehicle was being driven by a person without permission or authority of the owner/insured and thus, the vehicle was being used contrary to the terms and conditions of the insurance policy. It is contended that FIR was lodged after about seven days of the accident which itself raises doubts on the genuineness of the complaint. It is however conceded that the insurance policy is valid and effective on the date of accident. ISSUES : 6. Relief. 7. An application for assessment of disability was allowed vide order dated 14.02.2023 against which claimant was opined with 17% permanent physical disability qua his right hand vide communication dated 17.05.2023 addressed by Chairperson, Disability Board, Pt. Madan Mohan Malaviya Hospital. EVIDENCE 8. Matter was then listed for evidence before Local Commissioner. Injured examined himself as PW1 and tendered MACT No. 738/22 Arun Kataria vs. Rajender Singh Page No. 4 of 42 his evidentiary affidavit Ex.PW1/A and relied upon his Adhar Card, PAN Card, Discharge Summary, Treatment Papers and Medical Bills, as Ex.PW1/1 (colly). He also relied upon DAR as Ex.PW1/X. He was extensively cross-examined by Ld. Counsel for insurance company. None appeared on behalf of R-1 and R-2 to cross-examine the witness. Petitioner's evidence was closed upon request made by Ld. Counsel for claimant. Arun Katariya (Dar) vs Rajender Singh (290/21, Crp) on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34909065/ 3 9. None of the respondents chose to lead evidence in their defence. FINAL ARGUMENTS 10.
texts.arguments: Ld. Counsel for claimant argued that the accident happens only due to reckless driving of the Respondent no.1 at the time of accident. He also specified that injured was travelling in the Truck as an employee for loading / unloading of the bricks being transported. 11. Ld. Counsel for insurance company argued that there is AN unexplained delay of about seven days in registration of FIR. Further, injured was travelling in the Truck only as gratuitous passenger and therefore, cannot be taken to be covered under the policy, hence, complete exoneration has been sought against any liability towards the compensation DISCUSSION 12. 14. It has been held in catena of cases that negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view is to be taken. It has been further held that the proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to the proceedings in a Civil Suit and hence, strict rules of evidence are not applicable (support drawn from the case of Bimla Devi & Ors vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors [(2009) 13 SC 530, [Kaushnumma Begum and others v/s New India Assurance Company Limited, [2001 ACJ 421 SC], [National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pushpa Rana cited as [2009 ACJ 287 Del]. 15. PW1/ injured has testified about the factual matrix deposing about the circumstances as well as about the mode and Arun Katariya (Dar) vs Rajender Singh (290/21, Crp) on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34909065/ 4 manner of the accident with all clarity. There is no dispute about the identification of the vehicle or the driver thereof as the injured was travelling as labour on the very same vehicle. It is evident that he was trying to help for the smooth passage of the Truck upon the asking of the driver of said offending Truck when accident happened as said driver had put Truck in motion, without ensuring about the safety of person travelling therein. There is no evidence on record to show that the claimant tried to disentangle the cables and the branches of the tree on his own at MACT No. 738/22 Arun Kataria vs. Rajender Singh Page No. 6 of 42 his own will without any requirement and without asking of the driver of the Truck and thus, got injured on his risk and volition. No alternative explanation has been tendered by Respondent no.1 driver to explain the eventuality otherwise. Further, he only mentioned in the written statement as response to DAR that the injured was harmed while unloading the bricks, whereas he has not tried to substantiate his assertion. 16. PW1 has also tendered explanation as to why he did not report the matter to the police immediately after the accident. He also deposed that Truck Driver simply left him on his own and did not extend any help to even take him to the hospital. He also explained that it was on his undertaking to bear his medical expenses that he did not report the matter to police. The explanation tendered is convincing and cannot be held against him. The MLC tendered by him as part of police complaint specifically notes the manner of sustaining the injury which corroborates with the complaint and the affirmations made in the evidentiary affidavit. There seems to be no variance and contradictions in the testimony of injured PW1.Driver was also charge-sheeted for causing harm on account of rash driving on a public way. 17. Ld. counsel for insurance company argued at the stage of final arguments that the injured was travelling as gratuitous passenger and therefore insurance company does not entail any liability to make payment of compensation. The contention of gratuitous passenger has not been taken specifically in the written statement filed in response to DAR. Ld. Counsel for claimant has disputed the same and stated that the injured was travelling as an employee and therefore, insurance company has to own the responsibility to indemnify the insured against his liability towards the tort feasor. 32. The insurance policy has been admitted to be valid and effective as on the date of accident.
